lesson.title: Defence Can Change Before You Hit
lesson.hook: A wide ball does not decide your answer on its own. Your arrival can change the options.
lesson.memHTML: Need time? Buy it with height and depth.
lesson.tomorrow: When pulled wide, check how much time you need to recover. If you arrive early and see a real opening, a controlled change of direction may be available.
lesson.cue: Need time? Buy it with height and depth.

pro.label: Federer · Scramble first, decide again
pro.moment: At Indian Wells in 2006, Federer described his plan in surprisingly ordinary terms: scramble, keep balls in, use the short ball, then decide on the shot. Even his attacking game had a survival phase. Getting out of trouble gave him a new decision; it did not lock him into defending.
pro.read: Your next point: still stretched? Height and depth can buy recovery time. Arrived with control? Reassess what pressure you can apply.
pro.src: Roger Federer · Indian Wells press conference · 18 March 2006

steps.name: Choose your plan
steps.sit: Their ball takes you towards the sideline. Watch both players.
opts: Drive down the line, with margin
High and deep crosscourt, then recover
steps.payoff: Still travelling out? Give yourself time to get back.
steps.principle: Read your arrival as well as the ball and the opponent.
steps.why: The line is open, but you are still travelling to the ball. A higher, deeper crosscourt reply gives you more margin and flight time for recovery. It does not guarantee that they cannot attack.
steps.take: Still travelling out? Give yourself time to get back.

lines.A: An opening alone does not make the change of direction easy.
lines.B: The extra flight time can help you recover.

steps.name: Choose your plan
steps.sit: The same ball and opponent. Watch your arrival this time.
opts: Drive down the line, with margin
High and deep crosscourt, then recover
steps.payoff: Earlier arrival can open a choice; it does not require an attack.
steps.principle: Read your arrival as well as the ball and the opponent.
steps.why: You have reached the preparation position sooner and they are still across the court. The line can apply pressure with margin. High and deep is also a sound choice; the useful change is that you now have an option.
steps.take: Earlier arrival can open a choice; it does not require an attack.

lines.A: Earlier arrival makes the open line a reasonable pressure shot.
lines.B: Also sound: keep the margin and recover.

steps.name: Choose your plan
opts: High and deep crosscourt, then recover
Drive down the line, with margin
steps.payoff: Other wing, same question: how much time do you need?
steps.principle: Read your arrival as well as the ball and the opponent.
steps.why: You are still moving wide on the backhand side. The opponent is central. Choose height and depth to help your recovery instead of treating the sideline as an invitation to redirect.
steps.take: Other wing, same question: how much time do you need?

lines.A: Use the ball’s flight to help your recovery.
lines.B: A forced change of direction gives you less margin.

drill.name: Call the plan
drill.how: With a partner, vary the feed and your starting position. Before contact, call “pressure” or “buy time”. Afterwards, compare the call with your arrival, the ball and their position. Keep a useful cue; a won or lost point alone does not settle the decision.

readiness.evidence: Still travelling outward; recovery will take time.
Arrived earlier; the line remains open.
Other wing, still moving away from the court.
